claim: Foraminiferal shells are generated by chambers added in logarithmic-spiral succession with (near-)constant growth ratios, and the genera form a continuous geometric series transformable into one another.

dataset.name: Data from: Heterochronic origin of spherical fusulinid foraminifera in the Late Paleozoic
dataset.match: fusulinid foraminifera half-whorl outlines — same taxon class and variable as Thompson's von Moller Fusulina exemplar (p. 593); whorl-level, not septal-chamber-level

T1_geometric_succession.rule: median Pearson r(ln D, k) >= 0.98 and geometric beats arithmetic (BIC) in >= 80% of specimens

T2_near_constant_ratio.rule: median CV of successive ratios <= 0.15 AND in every genus the early/mid/late-third mean ratios differ by <= 10% of the mean (no systematic ontogenetic drift; Thompson p. 595 'small secondary fluctuation')

T3_fusulina_ratio_1_225.rule: Triticites (triticitid fusulinid, cf. von Moller's Fusulina) mean half-whorl ratio within 0.05 of 1.225

T4_continuous_series.rule: Monte-Carlo p >= 0.05 that a continuous (normal) ratio distribution produces an interior gap as large as observed, and every pair of genera adjacent in mean ratio has overlapping ranges

interpretation: Geometric (logarithmic-spiral) succession holds in every one of 106 fusulinid specimens (median r 0.99+, BIC prefers geometric over arithmetic growth in 100 %), and Thompson's exemplar group reproduces his number: Triticites half-whorl ratio 1.239 (95 % CI 1.232-1.245) vs von Moller/Thompson 1.225, whorl ratio 1.53 vs 1.5; the real thin section gives W = 1.49 by computer vision. The 'near-constant ratio' clause fails systematically for the inflated pseudoschwagerine genera (Pseudoschwagerina, Sphaeroschwagerina, Zellia, Robustoschwagerina): their ratio rises to ~1.45 in mid-ontogeny and falls to ~1.1, a heterochronic inflation (Shi 2021) far beyond Thompson's 'small secondary fluctuation'. The genus series is continuous in ratio (Monte-Carlo gap p = 0.74). Hence: supported for the geometric-succession core and for Thompson's own Fusulina numbers; refuted as a universal constant-ratio law — overall MIXED.
